trust.guarantees.title: What we guarantee
trust.guarantees.g1: One source of truth — every screen reads the same calculation engine; differences are only window/time, never the math.
trust.guarantees.g2: Honest blanks — missing data shows "—", never a fake 0% or 100%.
trust.guarantees.g3: No alert spam — one alert per incident, with an hourly safety cap.
trust.guarantees.g4: Shift-aware, capped downtime — no runaway stop can inflate the numbers.
trust.guarantees.g5: Auditable, not just claimed — these checks re-verify reconciliation live, on demand.

health.fix.toggle: What this means / How to fix
health.fix.downtime_cap.meaning: A stop was left running so long it's inflating your totals.
health.fix.downtime_cap.todo: Cap it here, then review it on the Downtime page.
health.fix.downtime_capacity.meaning: The recorded downtime is more than is physically possible.
health.fix.downtime_capacity.todo: It's on us — we'll recheck. If it stays, contact support.
health.fix.counter_drift.meaning: A finished job recorded a part count that its own cycle counter can't explain.
health.fix.counter_drift.cause: The counter was edited, or a job didn't close cleanly.
health.fix.counter_drift.todo: Open the job on the Work Orders page and review the counts.
health.fix.cycle_delivery.meaning: Some cycles a machine recorded never reached the cloud, with no sensor outage to explain it.
health.fix.cycle_delivery.cause: Messages were lost in transit — most are the one-time 06-15→06-18 outage, now fixed.
health.fix.cycle_delivery.todo: Accept the known past losses below; the numbers stay incomplete but accounted for. A new gap after this is rare and worth investigating.
health.fix.stuck_mold.meaning: A mold change was started and never marked finished.
health.fix.stuck_mold.cause: It wasn't closed on the floor.
health.fix.stuck_mold.todo: Mark it finished here, or review it on the Downtime page.
health.fix.clock_sync.meaning: A machine's clock is off, so its event times may be wrong.
health.fix.reader_link.meaning: A machine isn't recording data — its sensor is offline.
health.fix.reader_link.cause: The sensor was unplugged or is out of range.
health.fix.reader_link.todo: Check the sensor on that machine.
health.fix.screen_mismatch.meaning: A screen is showing a different number than the source.
health.fix.screen_mismatch.todo: Recheck. If it stays, contact support.
health.fix.financial_rates.meaning: Cost rates aren't set, so the peso impact can't be shown.
health.fix.financial_rates.cause: The cost rates haven't been entered.
health.fix.financial_rates.todo: Set the cost rates in Financial settings.
health.fix.confirm.stuckMold: Mark these mold changes as finished? This closes them so they stop affecting your totals.
health.fix.confirm.downtimeCap: Cap these stops at 12 hours? This corrects the stored values so they stop inflating your totals.
health.fix.confirm.cycleBackfill: Accept the current unexplained cycle gaps as known past data loss? This records them as reviewed so the board starts clean — a new gap after this will stand out.
health.fix.result.error: Couldn't apply the fix. Try again, or contact support.

workOrders.title: Work order completion
workOrders.subtitle: Every finished and active job, checked two ways: did the machine count parts correctly, and did all of its cycle data reach the cloud.
workOrders.error: Couldn't load work orders. Try refreshing.
workOrders.empty: No work orders to show yet.
workOrders.detail.counterOk: Yes — {cavities} cavities × {cycles} cycles ≈ {good} good parts. The machine's own counter is consistent.
workOrders.detail.counterError: No — {cavities} cavities × {cycles} cycles doesn't match the {good} good parts recorded. The machine's counter is inconsistent; investigate this job.
workOrders.detail.counterUnknown: Can't check — this job has no cavity count or its cycle counter wasn't recorded at close.
workOrders.detail.scrapTolerated: Scrap ({scrap}) is tracked separately and doesn't affect this check.
workOrders.detail.delivery: Did all the cycle data reach the cloud?
workOrders.delivery.complete: Yes — every cycle the machine recorded reached the cloud.
workOrders.delivery.recoverable: Some cycles haven't arrived yet. This job is still active and the edge is sending its backlog — the gap should close on its own.
workOrders.delivery.unexplained: Some cycles the machine recorded never reached the cloud, with no recorded sensor outage to explain it. This is unusual — review the job, then acknowledge it once accounted for.
workOrders.delivery.outage: Some cycles weren't recorded during a sensor outage on {date}. The machine kept running; the data for that window is gone.
workOrders.delivery.acceptedPreFix: Cycles lost before the data-delivery fix (the 06-15→06-18 outage). Reviewed and accepted as a known one-time loss.
workOrders.delivery.accepted: Reviewed and accepted by an admin.
workOrders.ack.hint: Records that this gap has been reviewed and accounted for.
workOrders.ack.forbidden: Only an admin can acknowledge a gap.
